sentences.text:
Smt. Pragya Borikar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7
November, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Jbp:55916
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Jabalpur

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pramod Kumar Agrawal

On The 7 th Of November, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 42684 of 2025
 Smt. Pragya Borikar
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Shishir Kumar Soni - Advocate for the applicant.

Shri Yogesh Dhande - Government Advocate for the resp
 Order

This is the first application filed on behalf of the applicant under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) for grant of anticipatory bail apprehending her arrest in relation to Crime No.363/2025 registered at Police Station - Lalbarra, District Balaghat (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B r/w 34 of IPC.
2.

As per the prosecution story, the allegation against the applicant is that she alongwith co-accused person committed fraud upon the complainant by selling the land to her, which was already sold to some other person.
The applicant has not verified the aforesaid factum.
Therefore, the offence has been registered against the applicant and co-accused under aforesaid offences.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is lady.
She NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:55916 2 MCRC-42684-2025 is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is submitted that the applicant is a government servant holding the post of Patwari.
It is further submitted that the spot map of the land was prepared in the presence of Sarpanch and other witnesses.
The said work has been done by the applicant in the official capacity.
She has only performed her duty.
There was no malafide intention on the part of applicant to commit the alleged offence.
There is no need of custodial interrogation of the applicant.
There is no criminal antecedents of the applicant.
The conclusion of trial will take considerable time.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant may be granted benefit of anticipatory bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for State has opposed the grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant and prayed for it's rejection.

sentences.text: 5. Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the anticipatory bail application filed by the applicant is allowed.

It is directed that if the applicant is arrested by the police then she shall be released on bail on her furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rs. Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Investigating Officer/Arresting Authority.

(e) She will further abide by the condition enumerated in sub-section (3) of Section 480 of the Cr.P.C.
